text:
acme_infra: Hey team — we've got streaming responses from our Dedicated cluster that are getting cut mid-response. Client sees a partial SSE payload, then the connection closes and the client reconnects which results in duplicated tokens and duplicate billing events. Happening behind our corporate TLS-inspecting proxy (MTU ~1400). Example request id: req_0a1b2c3d.

maria.l: Sorry you're seeing this. Can you share a minimal curl repro and the exact headers you send? Also any proxy vendor/version info?

acme_infra: Minimal repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream\" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-8k-dedicated","input":"stream test to reproduce fragmentation..."}'
```
Proxy is a corp TLS-inspect appliance (vendor: CorpProxyX 4.2). We can repro reliably when client is behind it; direct cloud clients do not hit the issue.

aj: Two likely vectors: MTU/fragmentation causing SSE boundary splits, and TLS-inspection re-chunking that strips or combines SSE delimiters ("\n\n"). Can you attach a tcpdump of a failing run (client <-> proxy and proxy <-> Redwood if possible)? Also does client use keepalive or send periodic heartbeats?

acme_infra: Attaching a short tcpdump excerpt (sanitized):
```
14:32:01.123456 IP proxy > redwood  Flags [P.], seq 12345:19600, ack 54321, win 65535, length 7255
14:32:01.124000 IP proxy > redwood  Flags [F.], seq 19600:19600, ack 54321, win 65535, length 0
```
We see a FIN right after a large packet — chunk looks like it contained an SSE event without the trailing double newline. Client got partial event then timed out and reconnected.

kevin: That tcpdump is a strong hint. When proxies aggressively close or re-chunk TCP with TLS inspect + MTU clamping, SSE delimiters can land mid-packet. Some clients treat partial data as a complete event or drop it. Two mitigation paths: (1) server/ingress reduce chunk size or add explicit per-event heartbeats so partials are recoverable, (2) client-side resume token to avoid double-billing on reconnect. We also need to check our billing logic: duplicate invoice on reconnect is not acceptable.

maria.l: Can you try this quick server-side repro script (run from a machine behind the proxy) — it emulates large SSE chunks to trigger fragmentation:
```python
# sse_repro.py
import time, sys, socket
s = socket.socket()
s.connect((\"api.redwood.example\", 443))  # use stunnel / proxy path if needed
# This is pseudo, actual TLS step omitted for brevity
for i in range(3):
    sys.stdout.write('data: ' + 'X'*8192 + '\\n\\n')
    sys.stdout.flush()
    time.sleep(1)
```
If that produces the cut behavior, it's consistent with MTU/proxy re-chunking.

acme_infra: Running it now, will attach PCAP. Also note client sets no explicit keepalive; default socket keepalive is enabled.

aj: On the Redwood ingress side we can also test with MTU artificially reduced to 1400, and run a TLS-inspect proxy (we have a replica). We'll try to reproduce. Meanwhile, immediate suggestions for you:
- Enable application-level SSE heartbeats every 10-15s. (server: send `:\n` comment lines)
- Ask your proxy team to disable aggressive connection close on mid-chunk or increase MSS.
- If possible, have client set TCP_NODELAY / no Nagle when streaming small writes, or reduce single-event size < 1KB.

kevin: Regarding billing duplicates: our back-end currently increments billed tokens on session start + per-chunk commit events. If a client reconnects without a resume token, it's treated as a new session. Short-term we'll issue credits for verified duplicates. Longer term we should bind billing to `session_id` or accept a `resume_token` to continue the same billing session.

thomas: I've pushed a temporary safeguard on the Dedicated cluster for this customer: idempotency by `client_parent_session_id` for 48 hours (prevents immediate double charge). We'll monitor for any regressions.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-042 - "Dedicated SSE mid-response cut + duplicate billing (ACME)" — assignee: @maria.l — priority: P2. Link: https://infra.redwood/INC-2026-042

maria.l: Next actions:
- acme_infra: provide full pcap and the exact curl command you used (with headers) and proxy vendor logs.
- Redwood (aj + kevin + thomas): try to reproduce in staging with MTU=1400 + TLS-inspect; validate we can reproduce and capture our ingress logs.
- Short-term mitigation: enable SSE heartbeats, reduce chunk sizes, client to use resume flow (we'll document resume header) so reconnects don't re-bill.

acme_infra: Uploading pcap and proxy logs to the shared folder now. Appreciate the fast turnaround. We can try the resume token approach — please share the header format.

maria.l: Resume header format (experimental): `Resume-Token: <token>` and `Parent-Session-Id: <client-supplied-id>`. We'll send full docs in the ticket. For now we recommend: keep heartbeat, smaller chunks, enable resume.

kevin: We'll also prepare a credit for duplicate charges tied to request ids you provide (req_0a1b2c3d etc.). Hoping to have reproduction results within 24h.

acme_infra: Thanks all — pcap uploaded. We'll test heartbeat + resume on our side and report back. :pray:

maria.l: Thanks — we'll update INC-2026-042 as we make progress.
